correctness.rationale: For all real q>1 and 0<lambda<1, ordered separated affine branches give the exact cumulative mass identity (1). Hurwitz zeta tails to two terms, uniformly in the within-cell coordinate, yield c^s(Q_lambda(a)-a)n^{-qs} with O(n^{-qs-1}) remainder. The positive coefficient c^s(1-lambda) at a=lambda proves optimality. The shift digits are independent; coupling rare visits to a binomial count incurs probability O(m^{-1/(qs-1)}), followed by an O(m^{-1}) Poisson approximation. Two nondegenerate parameter pairs passed numerical diagnostic replay. No infinite result relies on finite testing.
